name: Kruisjassen
description: Kruisjassen is a Dutch jass game played by four players in fixed partnerships, two against two. This format gives the game its name, which means 'cross-jass'. As played in the east of the Netherlands, it is one of the most straightforward forms of jass, simpler than the better known Klaverjassen. There is no bidding, trumps are chosen simply by turning a card at the end of the deal, and the result is determined by the value of cards taken in tricks.

history.origins: Kruisjassen developed in the eastern Netherlands as a simplified variant of the broader Jass family of games. The name refers to the cross-wise seating of partnerships. It emerged as a more accessible alternative to complex bidding games like Klaverjassen.
timeline: 19th Century: Jass games spread through the Netherlands from Swiss/French origins
Early 1900s: Kruisjassen emerges as distinct simplified variant in eastern Netherlands
Mid-20th Century: Becomes popular in cafe leagues and family settings
Present: Remains popular in Gelderland and eastern regions
history.cultural: Commonly played in Dutch cafes (bruine cafÃ©s) and at family gatherings. The straightforward rules make it a popular teaching game for introducing players to the Jass family.
history.evolution: The game simplified the Jass format by removing bidding and meld announcements, focusing purely on trick-taking and point accumulation. This made it faster and more accessible to casual players.

setup.players: Four players in fixed partnerships, two against two. Partners sit opposite each other.
setup.deck: 32-card French-suited pack (7 through Ace in each suit).
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles, offers to player on left to cut, then deals: 3 cards each, then 2 cards each, then 3 cards each. The last card (dealer's last card) is placed face up to determine trump suit, then taken into dealer's hand. Each player has 8 cards.

rules.objective: Win tricks containing high-value cards. Score game points by reaching point thresholds with your partner.
rules.gameplay:
1. **Leading**: Player to dealer's left leads to first trick. Any card may be led.
2. **Following Suit**: If a non-trump is led, players with that suit must either follow suit OR play a trump. A non-trump of a different suit can only be played if the player has no cards of the led suit.
3. **Trumping Rules**: When playing a trump on a non-trump lead, it must be higher than any trumps already played to the trick. A lower trump can only be played if the player has no option (hand consists entirely of lower trumps).
4. **Trump Led**: If a trump is led, other players must play trumps if they have them. Any trump may be played - no requirement to play higher.
5. **Winning Tricks**: Highest trump wins, or if no trumps, highest card of led suit. Winner leads to next trick.
keyRules: Trump Jack is worth 20 points, Trump Nine is worth 14 points
Need 100+ card points to score 2 game points
Win all tricks to score 5 game points

strategy.basic: Count points as they fall. Remember there are 146 total points, so you need 100 for the 2-point score. The last trick (5 points) can be decisive in close games.
strategy.intermediate: Trump Management: Save your trumps for when they can capture high-point cards. The trump Jack (20 points) and Nine (14 points) are crucial. Don't waste trumps on low-value tricks.
strategy.advanced: Void Creation: Try to exhaust one suit early so you can trump when that suit is led. This is especially powerful if you have several trumps. Signal to your partner through your lead choices - leading a low card often suggests strength in that suit or a desire for partner to take the trick.
tips: The trump Nine (14 points) is almost as valuable as an Ace - protect it.
If you have many trumps, lead them early to draw out opponents' trumps.
Pay attention to which high cards have been played to calculate remaining points.
Communication with your partner through lead choices is key - but no table talk!

variations.name: Fixed Length Game
variations.description: Play a fixed number of deals (e.g., 8 or 16) and add up card points. Team with higher grand total wins.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes only number of deals and win condition; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: Kruisjassen with Tik
variations.description: If a team reaches 50 card points during play, they may tap the table ('tik') to score 1 game point immediately. If both reach 50, first to tap wins. A team that taps and wins all tricks scores 6 game points.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Tik adds optional scoring moment; core engine and constants unchanged.

variations.name: Kruisjassen with Roem
variations.description: Adds meld points for card combinations held in hand: sequences (20-100 points) and four-of-a-kinds (100-200 points). Team with best roem scores for all their combinations. Also includes 'stuk' (K+Q of trumps) for 20 points.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Roem variant would need meldConfig; overrides not yet mapped to schema.

variations.name: All Tricks Bonus Tournament
variations.description: In tournament play, winning all 8 tricks scores an extra bonus of 100 card points (total 246).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Bonus applies only to scoring; no engine constant overrides.

scoring.description: Points from cards in tricks are converted to game points. First to 11 game points wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Kruisjassen is a straightforward Dutch jass game played in partnerships with no bidding and turned-card trumps.
